title: Archive — Previous Teaching
subtitle: Earlier studios, seminars, and computational-design pedagogy
coverAlt: Previous teaching archive featuring Morphing Skins
summary: An archive for earlier design studios and seminars. The current visual selection documents Morphing Skins, a Spring 2025 third-year design studio.
body: Morphing Skins reversed the conventional studio sequence by beginning with surface rather than site, program, or massing. Folding, cutting, curling, faceting, crumpling, triangulating, and tessellating were treated as tectonic systems capable of producing structure, enclosure, spatial depth, and light modulation.

Students first developed paper-based rule sets, physical studies, digital translations, and matrices of variation. They then expanded these systems into surface networks and massing studies before applying them to the Carolina Theatre site.

The final phase integrated envelope, structure, circulation, and program. Large physical models, plans, sections, elevations, renderings, and diagrams demonstrated how an outside-in design process could connect material experimentation with architectural resolution.
This archive remains available for additional earlier studios and seminars while Morphing Skins serves as its current featured teaching example.
